# Mean annual precipitation data extractions and interpolation

[Assigning 2015 Mean Annual Precipitation (MAP) to each sampling site’s coordinates]{.underline}\
Some sites had grass samples with nearby coordinates measured.\

Only (LTER?) certain sites had MAP (in mm) previously measured. To fill in the remaining data (and cross-referencing the congruence of the overlapping data), we integrated spatial point data (geographic coordinates) with CHELSA precipitation rasters.

Mean Annual Precipitation (MAP) for the year 2015 was derived from the CHELSAcruts dataset (Climatologies at High resolution for the Earth's Land Surface Areas), which provides high-resolution (\~1 km, 30 arc-second) monthly precipitation data. We downloaded the full set of 12 monthly precipitation rasters (GeoTIFF format) for the year 2015 from the CHELSA data repository (<https://www.envidat.ch/dataset/chelsacruts/resource/26958a2a-c7fa-4f16-82ce-57f2bbac59c8>; Identifier chelsacruts.26958a2a-c7fa-4f16-82ce-57f2bbac59c8, Issued date: June 23, 2020; Modified date: June 23, 2020). CHELSAcruts is a delta change monthly climate dataset for the years 1901-2016 for mean monthly maximum temperatures, mean monthly minimum temperatures, and monthly precipitation sum. The data was accessed using the URL (<https://envicloud.wsl.ch/#/?bucket=https%3A%2F%2Fos.zhdk.cloud.switch.ch%2Fchelsav1%2F&prefix=chelsa_cruts%2F> (Metadata last updated: September 19, 2024; Data last updated: October 29, 2018; Created: October 29, 2018; Accessed: March 26, 2025).

All raster data were processed using R (v4.4.3) with the raster (v3.6.31) and data.table (v1.17.0) packages. The 12 monthly CHELSA precipitation rasters for 2015 were loaded and stacked into a multilayer raster object. Annual precipitation for 2015 was computed by summing the 12 monthly layers using calc(..., sum) with na.rm = TRUE. Point-based extraction of precipitation values was performed using the extract() function from the raster package, which interpolates cell values at each sampling coordinate.

```{r, include=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library(raster)
library(data.table)

# mapping_coords_CHELSAcruts_prec2025.R

# 1. Load your coordinates file
site_coords_with_newMAP <- fread("../metadata/CHELSAcruts_2015/site_coords_with_MAP_2015_rasterout.csv")  # Ensure columns: latitude, longitude
```

```{r, echo=FALSE,message=FALSE, eval=F}
source("analyze_metadata_differences.R")

sample_data(Fun_wholecommunity)$MAP_2015 <- as.numeric(site_coords_with_newMAP$MAP_2015)

res_MAP_2015 <- analyze_metadata_differences(
  physeq_object = Fun_wholecommunity,
  group_var = "Fun_sor_clus2",
  filter = F,
  # exclude_vars = c("clus_sor_k10", "clus_sor_k10_new","Fun_sor_clus2", "SampleID","sample_name","X16S_ID")
  vars = "MAP_2015")  # Or leave NULL for all
# )


library(phyloseq)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggplot2)
library(glue)
library(effectsize)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(cowplot)
meta_df2 <- phylo2vegan_sd(Fun_wholecommunity)
test_var <- "MAP_2015"
group_var <- "Fun_sor_clus2"


df2 <- meta_df2 %>%
  subset(., select=c(get(test_var), get(group_var))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(test_var))

    x2 <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(df2[[test_var]]))
    is_numeric <- !all(is.na(x2))
    
    test_res <- tryCatch({
        df2[[test_var]] <- x2
        test <- wilcox.test(df2[[test_var]] ~ df2[[group_var]])
        eff <- effectsize::rank_biserial(df2[[test_var]], df2[[group_var]])
        pval_fmt <- format.pval(test$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .001)
        plot <- ggboxplot(df2, x = "Fun_sor_clus2", y = "MAP_2015", fill = "Fun_sor_clus2", palette = c("#8E0152","#7FBC41")) +
          stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", label.y.npc = "top") +
          theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
          theme(legend.position = "none",
                axis.text = element_text(color="black", size=11)) +
          labs(title = "MAP_2015", x = NULL, y = "MAP_2015")
        
        tibble(
          Variable = test_var,
          Type = "Numeric",
          Test = "Wilcoxon rank-sum",
          P_value = as.numeric(pval_fmt),
          Effect_size = round(eff$r_rank_biserial, 2),
          test_obj = list(test),
          effect_obj = list(eff),
          plot = list(plot)
        )
        
        results[[test_var]] <- test_res
})
    

          # --- Combine and filter ---
  res_df2 <- results %>%
     keep(~ all(c("P_value", "Variable") %in% names(.x))) #%>%
  #   bind_rows()
  # 
  # res_df2 <- test_res %>%
  #   mutate(P_value_numeric = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(P_value))) %>%
  #   arrange(P_value_numeric)
  

  # --- Print table ---
  print(
    res_df2$MAP_2015[,1:5] %>%
      # select(Variable, Type, Test, P_value, Effect_size) %>%
      knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Metadata features distinguishing F1 vs non-F1") %>%
      kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
  )
  
  # --- Plot
    print(cowplot::plot_grid(plot, ncol = 1))

```

# Comparing OTUs present in F1 vs non-F1

```{r venn-F1-vs-non-F1, include=FALSE,eval=TRUE}
library(ggVennDiagram)

meta <- data.frame(sample_data(Fun_wholecommunity))
groups <- unique(meta$Fun_sor_clus2)

# Get OTUs present (≥1 count) in each Fun_sor_clus2 group
taxa_lists <- setNames(lapply(groups, function(diet_group) {
  sample_ids <- rownames(meta[meta$Fun_sor_clus2 == diet_group, ])
  mat <- as(otu_table(Fun_wholecommunity)[, sample_ids, drop = FALSE], "matrix")
  rownames(mat)[rowSums(mat) >= 1]  # presence/absence filter
}), groups)
# str(taxa_lists)
      # List of 4
      #  $ Control-diet  : chr [1:375] "OTU58" "OTU191" "OTU89" ...
      #  $ HFD           : chr [1:269] "OTU58" "OTU191" "OTU89" ...
      #  $ HFD-LA        : chr [1:336] "OTU58" "OTU191" "OTU89" ...
      #  $ Villin-Cre-HFD: chr [1:287] "OTU58" "OTU191" "OTU89" ...

# Calculate Shared OTUs Between Two Groups
# Adjust to match actual names in your taxa_lists
groupF1 <- "F1"
groupnonF1 <- "non-F1"

shared_otus_F1_nonF1 <- intersect(
  taxa_lists[[groupF1]], taxa_lists[[groupnonF1]])
n_shared_F1_nonF1 <- length(shared_otus_F1_nonF1)

# Percent of each group
pctF1shared_F1_nonF1 <- round(
  100 * n_shared_F1_nonF1 / length(taxa_lists[[groupF1]]), 1)
pctnonF1shared_F1_nonF1 <- round(
  100 * n_shared_F1_nonF1 / length(taxa_lists[[groupnonF1]]), 1)

pairwise_note <- paste0(
  groupF1, " and ", groupnonF1, " share ", n_shared_F1_nonF1, " OTUs, comprising ",
  pctF1shared_F1_nonF1, "% and ", pctnonF1shared_F1_nonF1, "% of each, respectively"
)

# 2. Create Venn and process for plotting
res_venn <- Venn(taxa_lists)
venn_data <- process_data(res_venn)

# Define a scale factor
scale_factor <- 1.05  # You can tweak this as needed

# Apply to region edges, region labels, and set labels
region_data <- venn_regionedge(venn_data)
region_data$X <- region_data$X * scale_factor
region_data$Y <- region_data$Y * scale_factor

region_labels <- venn_regionlabel(venn_data)
region_labels$X <- region_labels$X * scale_factor
region_labels$Y <- region_labels$Y * scale_factor

set_labels <- venn_setlabel(venn_data)
# set_labels$X <- c(-1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5)  # spread them evenly
set_labels$X <- set_labels$X * scale_factor
set_labels$Y <- set_labels$Y * scale_factor

set_edges <- venn_setedge(venn_data)
set_edges$X <- set_edges$X * scale_factor
set_edges$Y <- set_edges$Y * scale_factor


# 2. Core OTUs
total_otus <- sum(region_labels$count)
core_taxa <- Reduce(intersect, taxa_lists)
core_count <- length(core_taxa)

# 3. Format labels: one decimal place
region_labels$label_fmt <- paste0(
  region_labels$count, "\n(",
  percent(region_labels$count / total_otus
          # , accuracy = 0.1
          ), ")"
)


# 4. Adjust fill scale for visibility (cap saturation)
max_count <- max(region_labels$count)
scale_limit <- ceiling(max_count * 0.8)


# 5. Final clean and print-optimized plot
Fun_sor_clus2_venn <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(aes(X, Y, group = id, fill = count),
               data = region_data) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    # option = "mako", direction = 1, name = "OTU count",
    ## trans = "log10",
    # limits = c(0, max(region_labels$count)*1.25), #oob = squish,
    option = "mako", direction = 1, name = "OTU count (log2)",
    trans = "log2",
    limits = c(512, max(region_labels$count)*2.4), #oob = squish,
    end = 0.15, # if direction = -1 this changes the lightest/lowest
    begin = 0.95,
    guide = guide_colorbar(
      barheight = 5, barwidth = 1.25,
      title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0
    )
  ) +

  geom_path(aes(X, Y, group = id), 
            data = set_edges, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(X, Y, label = name), 
            data = set_labels, size = 4.6, family = "Arial") +
  geom_label(
    aes(X, Y, label = label_fmt),
    data = region_labels,
    size = 2.8, label.size = 0.1, fill = "white",
    label.r = unit(0.12, "lines"), lineheight = 0.95,
    family = "Arial"
  ) +
  # annotate("text", x = -6, y = -5.5,
  annotate("text", x = -5.5, y = -5.5,
           label = paste("Core OTUs shared across both groups:", core_count, "(out of",total_otus,"total unique OTUs detected)"),
           hjust = 0.1, vjust = 0, size = 4.1, fontface = "italic", family = "Arial") +
  
  annotate("text", x = -6.9, y = -7,
         label = pairwise_note,
         hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = 4.1, family = "Arial", fontface = "italic")+

  # coord_fixed() +  # Keeps proportions tight
  # coord_fixed(clip = "off", xlim = c(-6, 6), ylim = c(-5, 5))+
  coord_cartesian(
  xlim = c(-6.5, 3),
  ylim = c(-10, 10),
  clip = "off") +
  
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 14, face = "plain"),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.18, .97),
    legend.justification = c("right", "top"),
    legend.box.just = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 50, b = 10, l = 25),
    text = element_text(family = "Arial")
  ) +
  labs(title = "All sites and grasses |\nShared and Unique OTUs within Fungal Assemblages Cohorts")

# get_plot_limits(Fun_sor_clus2_venn)
Fun_sor_clus2_venn

ggsave("../docs/figures/venn_diagrams/Fun_sor_clus2_venn.tiff", plot = Fun_sor_clus2_venn,
       width = 3.34*2.1, height = 2.8*1.8, dpi = 600, units = "in")
ggsave("../docs/figures/venn_diagrams/Fun_sor_clus2_venn.png", plot = Fun_sor_clus2_venn,
       width = 3.34*2.1, height = 2.8*1.8, dpi = 600, units = "in")
```

```{r venn-grass-F1, eval=FALSE}
region_data <- venn_regionedge(venn_data)
region_data$X <- region_data$X * scale_factor
region_data$Y <- region_data$Y * scale_factor

region_labels <- venn_regionlabel(venn_data)
region_labels$X <- region_labels$X * scale_factor
region_labels$Y <- region_labels$Y * scale_factor

set_labels <- venn_setlabel(venn_data)
# set_labels$X <- c(-1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5)  # spread them evenly
set_labels$X <- set_labels$X * scale_factor
set_labels$Y <- set_labels$Y * scale_factor

set_edges <- venn_setedge(venn_data)
set_edges$X <- set_edges$X * scale_factor
set_edges$Y <- set_edges$Y * scale_factor


# 2. Core OTUs
total_otus <- sum(region_labels$count)
core_taxa <- Reduce(intersect, taxa_lists)
core_count <- length(core_taxa)

# 3. Format labels: one decimal place


region_labels$label_fmt <- paste0(
  region_labels$count, "\n(",
  percent(region_labels$count / total_otus
          # , accuracy = 0.1
          ,format = "G", digits = 2
          ), ")"
)


# 4. Adjust fill scale for visibility (cap saturation)
max_count <- max(region_labels$count)
scale_limit <- ceiling(max_count * 0.8)


# 5. Final clean and print-optimized plot
F1_byGrass_venn <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(aes(X, Y, group = id, fill = count),
               data = region_data) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    # limits = c(0, max(region_labels$count)*1.25), #oob = squish,
    option = "mako", direction = 1, name = "OTU count (log2)",
    trans = "log2",
    limits = c(2, max(region_labels$count)*2.5), #oob = squish,
    end = 0.15, # if direction = -1 this changes the lightest/lowest
    begin = 0.95,
    guide = guide_colorbar(
      barheight = 5, barwidth = 1.25,
      title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0
    )
  ) +

  geom_path(aes(X, Y, group = id), 
            data = set_edges, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(X, Y, label = name), 
            data = set_labels, size = 4.6, family = "Arial") +
  geom_label(
    aes(X, Y, label = label_fmt), data = region_labels,
    size = 2.8, label.size = 0.1, fill = "white",
    label.r = unit(0.12, "lines"), lineheight = 0.95, family = "Arial"
  ) +

  annotate("text", x = 45.5, y = -25,
           label = paste("Core OTUs shared across all grasses:", core_count, "(out of",total_otus,"total unique OTUs detected)"),
           hjust = 0.1, vjust = 0, size = 4.1, fontface = "italic", family = "Arial") +
  
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = -120,
           label = paste(
             "These core OTUs constitute the majority of communities:\n",
             percent(sum(abundANGE) / sum(totalANGE), digits = 1),
             " of the mean relative abundance within ANGE, ", 
             percent(sum(abundBOGR) / sum(totalBOGR), digits = 1), " of BOGR,\n", 
             percent(sum(abundSCSC) / sum(totalSCSC), digits = 1), " of SCSC, ", 
             percent(sum(abundBOER) / sum(totalBOER), digits = 1), " of BOER, and ", 
             percent(sum(abundBUDA) / sum(totalBUDA), digits = 1), " of BUDA", 
             sep = ""), hjust = 0, vjust = 0, 
           size = 3.5, family = "Arial", fontface = "italic")+

  # annotate("text", x = 0, y = -90,
  #        label = pairwise_note,
  #        hjust = 0.1, vjust = 0, size = 4.1, family = "Arial", fontface = "italic")+

  # coord_fixed() +  # Keeps proportions tight
  # coord_fixed(clip = "off", xlim = c(-6, 6), ylim = c(-5, 5))+
  coord_cartesian(
  xlim = c(-0, 1000),
  ylim = c(-100, 1000),
  clip = "off") +
  
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 14, face = "plain"),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(1.1, .97),
    legend.justification = c("right", "top"),
    legend.box.just = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 60, b = 5, l = 15),
    text = element_text(family = "Arial")
  ) +
  labs(title = "F1 Sites | Shared and Unique OTUs within Grass Hosts")

# get_plot_limits(F1_byGrass_venn)
F1_byGrass_venn

ggsave("../docs/figures/venn_diagrams/F1_byGrass_venn.tiff", plot = F1_byGrass_venn,
       width = 3.34*2.1, height = 2.8*2.5, dpi = 600, units = "in")
ggsave("../docs/figures/venn_diagrams/F1_byGrass_venn.png", plot = F1_byGrass_venn,
       width = 3.34*2.5, height = 2.8*2.9, dpi = 600, units = "in")
```

```{r venn-grass-non-F1, eval=FALSE}
library(ggVennDiagram)

nonF1_phylo<-subset_samples(Fun_wholecommunity,Fun_sor_clus2=="non-F1")
nonF1_phylo <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(nonF1_phylo) > 0, nonF1_phylo)

groups <- unique(meta$Grass)

# Get OTUs present (≥1 count) in each Fun_sor_clus2 group
taxa_lists <- setNames(lapply(groups, function(group) {
  sample_ids <- rownames(meta[meta$Grass == group, ])
  mat <- as(otu_table(phylo_venn)[, sample_ids, drop = FALSE], "matrix")
  rownames(mat)[rowSums(mat) >= 1]  # presence/absence filter
}), groups)

groupBOER <- "BOER"
groupBUDA <- "BUDA"
groupSCSC <- "SCSC"

samplesBOER <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupBOER, ])

samplesSCSC <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupSCSC, ])

# CORE:  relative abundance: subset, sum across samples, divide by total

abundBOGR <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesBOGR, drop = FALSE])
abundBOER <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesBOER, drop = FALSE])
abundBUDA <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesBUDA, drop = FALSE])
abundSCSC <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesSCSC, drop = FALSE])


# SHARED: Normalize by total abundance in group
totalANGE <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesANGE, drop = FALSE])
totalBOGR <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesBOGR, drop = FALSE])
totalBOER <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesBOER, drop = FALSE])
totalBUDA <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesBUDA, drop = FALSE])
totalSCSC <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesSCSC, drop = FALSE])
```

```{r venn-grass-F3-n3, eval=FALSE}
                         # "BOER","BOGR",
                         "BUDA","SCSC")]

# Calculate Shared OTUs Between Two Groups
# Adjust to match actual names in your taxa_lists
groupANGE <- "ANGE"
groupBOGR <- "BOGR"
groupBOER <- "BOER"
groupBUDA <- "BUDA"
groupSCSC <- "SCSC"

# Get sample IDs for each group
samplesANGE <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupANGE, ])
# samplesBOGR <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupBOGR, ])
# samplesBOER <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupBOER, ])
samplesBUDA <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupBUDA, ])
samplesSCSC <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupSCSC, ])


# Extract abundance matrices
otu_mat <- as(otu_table(phylo_venn), "matrix")

core_taxa <- Reduce(intersect, taxa_lists)

# CORE:  relative abundance: subset, sum across samples, divide by total
abundANGE <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesANGE, drop = FALSE])
# abundBOGR <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesBOGR, drop = FALSE])
# abundBOER <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesBOER, drop = FALSE])
abundBUDA <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesBUDA, drop = FALSE])
abundSCSC <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesSCSC, drop = FALSE])


# SHARED: Normalize by total abundance in group
totalANGE <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesANGE, drop = FALSE])
# totalBOGR <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesBOGR, drop = FALSE])
# totalBOER <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesBOER, drop = FALSE])
totalBUDA <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesBUDA, drop = FALSE])
totalSCSC <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesSCSC, drop = FALSE])

# SHARED: Sum all shared across samples and normalize
# pctANGEshared_core <- round(100 * sum(abundANGE) / sum(totalANGE), 1)
# pctBOGRshared_core <- round(100 * sum(abundBOGR) / sum(totalBOGR), 1)
# pctBOGRshared_core <- round(100 * sum(abundBOGR) / sum(totalBOGR), 1)
# pctBOGRshared_core <- round(100 * sum(abundBOGR) / sum(totalBOGR), 1)
# pctBOGRshared_core <- round(100 * sum(abundBOGR) / sum(totalBOGR), 1)


# shared_otus_ANGE_BOGR <- intersect(
#   taxa_lists[[groupANGE]], taxa_lists[[groupBOGR]])
# n_shared_ANGE_BOGR <- length(shared_otus_ANGE_BOGR)

# Percent of each group
# pctANGEshared_ANGE_BOGR <- round(
#   100 * n_shared_ANGE_BOGR / length(taxa_lists[[groupANGE]]), 1)
# pctBOGRshared_ANGE_BOGR <- round(
#   100 * n_shared_ANGE_BOGR / length(taxa_lists[[groupBOGR]]), 1)

# pairwise_note <- paste0(
#   groupANGE, " and ", groupBOGR, " share ", n_shared_ANGE_BOGR, " OTUs, comprising ",
#   pctANGEshared_ANGE_BOGR, "% and ", pctBOGRshared_ANGE_BOGR, "% of each, respectively"
# )

# 2. Create Venn and process for plotting
res_venn <- Venn(taxa_lists)
venn_data <- process_data(res_venn)

# Define a scale factor
scale_factor <- 1.05  # You can tweak this as needed

# Apply to region edges, region labels, and set labels
region_data <- venn_regionedge(venn_data)
region_data$X <- region_data$X * scale_factor
region_data$Y <- region_data$Y * scale_factor

region_labels <- venn_regionlabel(venn_data)
region_labels$X <- region_labels$X * scale_factor
region_labels$Y <- region_labels$Y * scale_factor

set_labels <- venn_setlabel(venn_data)
# set_labels$X <- c(-1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5)  # spread them evenly
set_labels$X <- set_labels$X * scale_factor
set_labels$Y <- set_labels$Y * scale_factor

set_edges <- venn_setedge(venn_data)
set_edges$X <- set_edges$X * scale_factor
set_edges$Y <- set_edges$Y * scale_factor


# 2. Core OTUs
total_otus <- sum(region_labels$count)
core_taxa <- Reduce(intersect, taxa_lists)
core_count <- length(core_taxa)

# 3. Format labels: one decimal place


region_labels$label_fmt <- paste0(
  region_labels$count, "\n(",
  percent(region_labels$count / total_otus
          # , accuracy = 0.1
          ,format = "G", digits = 3
          ), ")"
)


# 4. Adjust fill scale for visibility (cap saturation)
max_count <- max(region_labels$count)
scale_limit <- ceiling(max_count * 0.8)


# 5. Final clean and print-optimized plot
F3_byGrass_venn <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(aes(X, Y, group = id, fill = count),
               data = region_data) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    # limits = c(0, max(region_labels$count)*1.25), #oob = squish,
    option = "mako", direction = 1, name = "OTU count (log2)",
    trans = "log2",
    limits = c(2, max(region_labels$count)*2.5), #oob = squish,
    end = 0.15, # if direction = -1 this changes the lightest/lowest
    begin = 0.95,
    guide = guide_colorbar(
      barheight = 5, barwidth = 1.25,
      title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0
    )
  ) +

  geom_path(aes(X, Y, group = id), 
            data = set_edges, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(X, Y, label = name), 
            data = set_labels, size = 4.6, family = "Arial") +
  geom_label(
    aes(X, Y, label = label_fmt), data = region_labels,
    size = 2.8, label.size = 0.1, fill = "white",
    label.r = unit(0.12, "lines"), lineheight = 0.95, family = "Arial"
  ) +

  annotate("text", x = -3.85, y = -10,
           label = paste("Core OTUs shared across all grasses:", core_count, "(out of",total_otus,"total unique OTUs detected)"),
           hjust = 0.1, vjust = 0, size = 4.1, fontface = "italic", family = "Arial") +
  
  annotate("text", x = -3.8, y = -11.2,
           label = paste(
             "These core OTUs constitute a variable proportion of communities:\n",
             percent(sum(abundANGE) / sum(totalANGE), digits = 1),
             " of the mean relative abundance within ANGE, ", 
             # percent(sum(abundBOGR) / sum(totalBOGR), digits = 1), " of BOGR,\n", 
             percent(sum(abundSCSC) / sum(totalSCSC), digits = 1), " of SCSC, ", 
             # percent(sum(abundBOER) / sum(totalBOER), digits = 1), " of BOER, and ", 
             percent(sum(abundBUDA) / sum(totalBUDA), digits = 1), " of BUDA", 
             sep = ""), hjust = 0, vjust = 0, 
           size = 3.5, family = "Arial", fontface = "italic")+

  # annotate("text", x = 0, y = -90,
  #        label = pairwise_note,
  #        hjust = 0.1, vjust = 0, size = 4.1, family = "Arial", fontface = "italic")+

  # coord_fixed() +  # Keeps proportions tight
  # coord_fixed(clip = "off", xlim = c(-6, 6), ylim = c(-5, 5))+
  coord_cartesian(
  # xlim = c(-0, 1000),
  # ylim = c(-100, 1000),
  clip = "off") +
  
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 14, face = "plain"),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(1.16, .93),
    legend.justification = c("right", "top"),
    legend.box.just = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 85, b = 5, l = 15),
    text = element_text(family = "Arial")
  ) +
  labs(title = "F3 Sites | Shared and Unique OTUs within Grass Hosts")

# get_plot_limits(F3_byGrass_venn)
F3_byGrass_venn

ggsave("../docs/figures/venn_diagrams/F3_byGrass_venn.tiff", plot = F3_byGrass_venn,
       width = 3.34*2.1, height = 2.8*2.5, dpi = 600, units = "in")
ggsave("../docs/figures/venn_diagrams/F3_byGrass_venn.png", plot = F3_byGrass_venn,
       width = 3.34*2.5, height = 2.8*2.3, dpi = 600, units = "in")
```

```{r venn-grass-F4-n4, eval=FALSE}
    limits = c(2, max(region_labels$count)*2.5), #oob = squish,
    end = 0.15, # if direction = -1 this changes the lightest/lowest
    begin = 0.95,
    guide = guide_colorbar(
      barheight = 5, barwidth = 1.25,
      title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0
    )
  ) +

  geom_path(aes(X, Y, group = id), 
            data = set_edges, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(X, Y, label = name), 
            data = set_labels, size = 4.6, family = "Arial") +
  geom_label(
    aes(X, Y, label = label_fmt), data = region_labels,
    size = 2.8, label.size = 0.1, fill = "white",
    label.r = unit(0.12, "lines"), lineheight = 0.95, family = "Arial"
  ) +

  annotate("text", x = 45.5, y = -25,
           label = paste("Core OTUs shared across all grasses:", core_count, "(out of",total_otus,"total unique OTUs detected)"),
           hjust = 0.1, vjust = 0, size = 4.1, fontface = "italic", family = "Arial") +
  
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = -120,
           label = paste(
             "These core OTUs constitute the majority of communities:\n",
             percent(sum(abundANGE) / sum(totalANGE), digits = 1),
             " of the mean relative abundance within ANGE, ", 
             percent(sum(abundBOGR) / sum(totalBOGR), digits = 1), " of BOGR,\n", 
             percent(sum(abundSCSC) / sum(totalSCSC), digits = 1), " of SCSC, and ", 
             # percent(sum(abundBOER) / sum(totalBOER), digits = 1), " of BOER, and ", 
             percent(sum(abundBUDA) / sum(totalBUDA), digits = 1), " of BUDA", 
             sep = ""), hjust = 0, vjust = 0, 
           size = 3.5, family = "Arial", fontface = "italic")+

  # annotate("text", x = 0, y = -90,
  #        label = pairwise_note,
  #        hjust = 0.1, vjust = 0, size = 4.1, family = "Arial", fontface = "italic")+

  # coord_fixed() +  # Keeps proportions tight
  # coord_fixed(clip = "off", xlim = c(-6, 6), ylim = c(-5, 5))+
  coord_cartesian(
  xlim = c(-0, 1000),
  ylim = c(-100, 1000),
  clip = "off") +
  
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 14, face = "plain"),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(1.1, .97),
    legend.justification = c("right", "top"),
    legend.box.just = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 60, b = 5, l = 15),
    text = element_text(family = "Arial")
  ) +
  labs(title = "F4 Sites | Shared and Unique OTUs within Grass Hosts")
```

```{r venn-grass-F6-n4, eval=FALSE}
library(ggVennDiagram)

# only ANGE BOGR BUDA SCSC

F6_phylo<-subset_samples(Fun_wholecommunity,Fun_sor_clusters=="F6")
F6_phylo <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(F6_phylo) > 0, F6_phylo)

phylo_venn <- F6_phylo

meta <- data.frame(sample_data(phylo_venn))
groups <- unique(meta$Grass)

# Get OTUs present (≥1 count) in each Fun_sor_clusters group
taxa_lists <- setNames(lapply(groups, function(group) {
  sample_ids <- rownames(meta[meta$Grass == group, ])
  mat <- as(otu_table(phylo_venn)[, sample_ids, drop = FALSE], "matrix")
  rownames(mat)[rowSums(mat) >= 1]  # presence/absence filter
}), groups)

# reorder grasses
taxa_lists<-taxa_lists[c("ANGE",
                         # "BOER",
                         "BOGR","BUDA","SCSC")]

# str(taxa_lists)

# Calculate Shared OTUs Between Two Groups
# Adjust to match actual names in your taxa_lists
groupANGE <- "ANGE"
groupBOGR <- "BOGR"
groupBOER <- "BOER"
groupBUDA <- "BUDA"
groupSCSC <- "SCSC"

# Get sample IDs for each group
samplesANGE <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupANGE, ])
samplesBOGR <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupBOGR, ])
# samplesBOER <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupBOER, ])
samplesBUDA <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupBUDA, ])
samplesSCSC <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupSCSC, ])


# Extract abundance matrices
otu_mat <- as(otu_table(phylo_venn), "matrix")

core_taxa <- Reduce(intersect, taxa_lists)

# CORE:  relative abundance: subset, sum across samples, divide by total
abundANGE <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesANGE, drop = FALSE])
abundBOGR <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesBOGR, drop = FALSE])
# abundBOER <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesBOER, drop = FALSE])
abundBUDA <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesBUDA, drop = FALSE])
abundSCSC <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesSCSC, drop = FALSE])


# SHARED: Normalize by total abundance in group
totalANGE <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesANGE, drop = FALSE])
totalBOGR <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesBOGR, drop = FALSE])
# totalBOER <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesBOER, drop = FALSE])
totalBUDA <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesBUDA, drop = FALSE])
totalSCSC <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesSCSC, drop = FALSE])

# 2. Create Venn and process for plotting
res_venn <- Venn(taxa_lists)
venn_data <- process_data(res_venn)

# Define a scale factor
scale_factor <- 1.05  # You can tweak this as needed

# Apply to region edges, region labels, and set labels
region_data <- venn_regionedge(venn_data)
region_data$X <- region_data$X * scale_factor
region_data$Y <- region_data$Y * scale_factor

region_labels <- venn_regionlabel(venn_data)
region_labels$X <- region_labels$X * scale_factor
region_labels$Y <- region_labels$Y * scale_factor

set_labels <- venn_setlabel(venn_data)
# set_labels$X <- c(-1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5)  # spread them evenly
set_labels$X <- set_labels$X * scale_factor
set_labels$Y <- set_labels$Y * scale_factor

set_edges <- venn_setedge(venn_data)
set_edges$X <- set_edges$X * scale_factor
set_edges$Y <- set_edges$Y * scale_factor


# 2. Core OTUs
total_otus <- sum(region_labels$count)
core_taxa <- Reduce(intersect, taxa_lists)
core_count <- length(core_taxa)

# 3. Format labels: one decimal place


region_labels$label_fmt <- paste0(
  region_labels$count, "\n(",
  percent(region_labels$count / total_otus
          # , accuracy = 0.1
          ,format = "G", digits = 2
          ), ")"
)


# 4. Adjust fill scale for visibility (cap saturation)
max_count <- max(region_labels$count)
scale_limit <- ceiling(max_count * 0.8)


# 5. Final clean and print-optimized plot
F6_byGrass_venn <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(aes(X, Y, group = id, fill = count),
               data = region_data) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "mako", direction = 1, name = "OTU count (log2)",
    trans = "log2",
    limits = c(2, max(region_labels$count)*2.5), #oob = squish,
    end = 0.15, # if direction = -1 this changes the lightest/lowest
    begin = 0.95,
    guide = guide_colorbar(
      barheight = 5, barwidth = 1.25,
      title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0)) +

  geom_path(aes(X, Y, group = id), 
            data = set_edges, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(X, Y, label = name), 
            data = set_labels, size = 4.6, family = "Arial") +
  geom_label(
    aes(X, Y, label = label_fmt), data = region_labels,
    size = 2.8, label.size = 0.1, fill = "white",
    label.r = unit(0.12, "lines"), lineheight = 0.95, family = "Arial") +

  annotate("text", x = 0.15, y = 0.15,
           label = paste("Core OTUs shared across all grasses:", core_count, "(out of",total_otus,"total unique OTUs detected)"),
           hjust = 0.1, vjust = 0, size = 4.1, fontface = "italic", family = "Arial") +
  
  annotate("text", x = 0.1, y = 0.05,
           label = paste(
             "These core OTUs constitute a variable but small proportion of communities:\n",
             percent(sum(abundANGE) / sum(totalANGE), digits = 1),
             " of the mean relative abundance within ANGE, ", 
             percent(sum(abundBOGR) / sum(totalBOGR), digits = 1), " of BOGR,\n", 
             percent(sum(abundBUDA) / sum(totalBUDA), digits = 1), " of BUDA, and ", 
             percent(sum(abundSCSC) / sum(totalSCSC), digits = 1), " of SCSC", 
             # percent(sum(abundBOER) / sum(totalBOER), digits = 1), " of BOER, and ", 
             sep = ""), hjust = 0, vjust = 0, 
           size = 3.5, family = "Arial", fontface = "italic")+

  # annotate("text", x = 0, y = -90,
  #        label = pairwise_note,
  #        hjust = 0.1, vjust = 0, size = 4.1, family = "Arial", fontface = "italic")+

  # coord_fixed() +  # Keeps proportions tight
  # coord_fixed(clip = "off", xlim = c(-6, 6), ylim = c(-5, 5))+
  coord_cartesian(
  # xlim = c(-0, 1000),
  # ylim = c(-100, 1000),
  clip = "off") +
  
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 14, face = "plain"),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(1.1, .45),
    legend.justification = c("right", "top"),
    legend.box.just = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 60, b = 5, l = 15),
    text = element_text(family = "Arial")
  ) +
  labs(title = "F6 Sites | Shared and Unique OTUs within Grass Hosts")

# get_plot_limits(F6_byGrass_venn)
F6_byGrass_venn

ggsave("../docs/figures/venn_diagrams/F6_byGrass_venn.tiff", plot = F6_byGrass_venn,
       width = 3.34*2.1, height = 2.8*2.5, dpi = 600, units = "in")
ggsave("../docs/figures/venn_diagrams/F6_byGrass_venn.png", plot = F6_byGrass_venn,
       width = 3.34*2.1, height = 2.8*2.2, dpi = 600, units = "in")
```

```{r venn-grass-F9-n4, eval=FALSE}
library(ggVennDiagram)

# only BOER BOGR BUDA SCSC

F9_phylo<-subset_samples(Fun_wholecommunity,Fun_sor_clusters=="F9")
F9_phylo <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(F9_phylo) > 0, F9_phylo)

phylo_venn <- F9_phylo

meta <- data.frame(sample_data(phylo_venn))
groups <- unique(meta$Grass)

# Get OTUs present (≥1 count) in each Fun_sor_clusters group
taxa_lists <- setNames(lapply(groups, function(group) {
  sample_ids <- rownames(meta[meta$Grass == group, ])
  mat <- as(otu_table(phylo_venn)[, sample_ids, drop = FALSE], "matrix")
  rownames(mat)[rowSums(mat) >= 1]  # presence/absence filter
}), groups)

# reorder grasses
taxa_lists<-taxa_lists[c(#"ANGE",
  "SCSC","BOER","BOGR","BUDA")]

# str(taxa_lists)

# Calculate Shared OTUs Between Two Groups
# Adjust to match actual names in your taxa_lists
groupANGE <- "ANGE"
groupBOGR <- "BOGR"
groupBOER <- "BOER"
groupBUDA <- "BUDA"
groupSCSC <- "SCSC"

# Get sample IDs for each group
# samplesANGE <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupANGE, ])
samplesBOGR <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupBOGR, ])
samplesBOER <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupBOER, ])
samplesBUDA <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupBUDA, ])
samplesSCSC <- rownames(sample_data(phylo_venn)[sample_data(phylo_venn)$Grass == groupSCSC, ])


# Extract abundance matrices
otu_mat <- as(otu_table(phylo_venn), "matrix")

core_taxa <- Reduce(intersect, taxa_lists)

# CORE:  relative abundance: subset, sum across samples, divide by total
# abundANGE <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesANGE, drop = FALSE])
abundBOGR <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesBOGR, drop = FALSE])
abundBOER <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesBOER, drop = FALSE])
abundBUDA <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesBUDA, drop = FALSE])
abundSCSC <- colSums(otu_mat[core_taxa, samplesSCSC, drop = FALSE])


# SHARED: Normalize by total abundance in group
# totalANGE <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesANGE, drop = FALSE])
totalBOGR <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesBOGR, drop = FALSE])
totalBOER <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesBOER, drop = FALSE])
totalBUDA <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesBUDA, drop = FALSE])
totalSCSC <- colSums(otu_mat[, samplesSCSC, drop = FALSE])

# 2. Create Venn and process for plotting
res_venn <- Venn(taxa_lists)
venn_data <- process_data(res_venn)

# Define a scale factor
scale_factor <- 1.05  # You can tweak this as needed

# Apply to region edges, region labels, and set labels
region_data <- venn_regionedge(venn_data)
region_data$X <- region_data$X * scale_factor
region_data$Y <- region_data$Y * scale_factor

region_labels <- venn_regionlabel(venn_data)
region_labels$X <- region_labels$X * scale_factor
region_labels$Y <- region_labels$Y * scale_factor

set_labels <- venn_setlabel(venn_data)
# set_labels$X <- c(-1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5)  # spread them evenly
set_labels$X <- set_labels$X * scale_factor
set_labels$Y <- set_labels$Y * scale_factor

set_edges <- venn_setedge(venn_data)
set_edges$X <- set_edges$X * scale_factor
set_edges$Y <- set_edges$Y * scale_factor


# 2. Core OTUs
total_otus <- sum(region_labels$count)
core_taxa <- Reduce(intersect, taxa_lists)
core_count <- length(core_taxa)

# 3. Format labels: one decimal place


region_labels$label_fmt <- paste0(
  region_labels$count, "\n(",
  percent(region_labels$count / total_otus
          # , accuracy = 0.1
          ,format = "G", digits = 2
          ), ")"
)


# 4. Adjust fill scale for visibility (cap saturation)
max_count <- max(region_labels$count)
scale_limit <- ceiling(max_count * 0.8)


# 5. Final clean and print-optimized plot

  geom_polygon(aes(X, Y, group = id, fill = count),

  scale_fill_viridis_c(
```

# Fungal vs. bacterial dissimilarity {.tabset}

## Scatterplots of fungal vs. bacterial dissimilarities

```{r prepare-pairwise-dissimilarities, include=FALSE,eval=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)

# Helper function to convert dist object to data.frame
dist_to_df <- function(d, label = "value") {
  mat <- as.matrix(d)
  df <- as.data.frame(as.table(mat), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  df <- df %>% filter(Var1 < Var2)  # lower triangle only
  colnames(df) <- c("Sample1", "Sample2", label)
  return(df)
}

# Required mapping tables
bac_id_map <- dplyr::select(sd, SampleID, X16S_ID)
sample_map <- dplyr::select(sd, SampleID, Site, Fun_sor_clus2, Fun_sor_clusters)

# Fungal dissimilarities
fun_f1_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(betapart_results[["Fun"]][["Fun_sor_clus2"]][["pairwise"]][["F1_Fun"]]$beta.sor))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(as.character(Var1) < as.character(Var2)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Sample1 = Var1, Sample2 = Var2, Fun_beta_sor = Freq) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Group = "F1")

fun_nonf1_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(betapart_results[["Fun"]][["Fun_sor_clus2"]][["pairwise"]][["non-F1_Fun"]]$beta.sor))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(as.character(Var1) < as.character(Var2)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Sample1 = Var1, Sample2 = Var2, Fun_beta_sor = Freq) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Group = "non-F1")

# Bacterial dissimilarities (map X16S_ID to SampleID)
bac_f1_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(betapart_results[["Bac"]][["Fun_sor_clus2"]][["pairwise"]][["F1_Bac"]]$beta.sor))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(as.character(Var1) < as.character(Var2)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(X1 = Var1, X2 = Var2, Bac_beta_sor = Freq) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(bac_id_map, by = c("X1" = "X16S_ID")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Sample1 = SampleID) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(bac_id_map, by = c("X2" = "X16S_ID")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Sample2 = SampleID) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample1, Sample2, Bac_beta_sor)

bac_nonf1_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(betapart_results[["Bac"]][["Fun_sor_clus2"]][["pairwise"]][["non-F1_Bac"]]$beta.sor))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(as.character(Var1) < as.character(Var2)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(X1 = Var1, X2 = Var2, Bac_beta_sor = Freq) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(bac_id_map, by = c("X1" = "X16S_ID")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Sample1 = SampleID) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(bac_id_map, by = c("X2" = "X16S_ID")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Sample2 = SampleID) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample1, Sample2, Bac_beta_sor)

# Join Fun + Bac dissimilarities
f1_df <- dplyr::inner_join(fun_f1_df, bac_f1_df, by = c("Sample1", "Sample2"))

  # non-F1
  shared_levels <- union(levels(fun_nonf1_df$Sample1), levels(bac_nonf1_df$Sample1))
  all_sample_levels <- union(
  levels(fun_nonf1_df$Sample1),
  levels(bac_nonf1_df$Sample1)
)
  
  fun_nonf1_df <- fun_nonf1_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Sample1 = factor(Sample1, levels = all_sample_levels),
    Sample2 = factor(Sample2, levels = all_sample_levels)
  )
    fun_nonf1_df %>% dplyr::filter(Sample1 %in% nonf1_hpg_samples, Sample2 %in% nonf1_hpg_samples) %>% dplyr::count()
    
    
  bac_nonf1_df <- bac_nonf1_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Sample1 = factor(Sample1, levels = all_sample_levels),
    Sample2 = factor(Sample2, levels = all_sample_levels)
  )
      bac_nonf1_df %>% dplyr::filter(Sample1 %in% nonf1_hpg_samples, Sample2 %in% nonf1_hpg_samples) %>% dplyr::count()
    
  
      # Add join key (order-independent)
      fun_nonf1_df <- fun_nonf1_df %>%
        dplyr::mutate(Pair = paste0(pmin(as.character(Sample1),
                                         as.character(Sample2)), "_",
                                    pmax(as.character(Sample1),
                                         as.character(Sample2))))
      
      bac_nonf1_df <- bac_nonf1_df %>%
        dplyr::mutate(Pair = paste0(pmin(as.character(Sample1),
                                         as.character(Sample2)), "_",
                                    pmax(as.character(Sample1),
                                         as.character(Sample2))))
      
      # Now join by Pair only
      nonf1_df <- dplyr::inner_join(fun_nonf1_df, bac_nonf1_df, by = "Pair") %>%
        dplyr::select(Sample1 = Sample1.x, Sample2 = Sample2.x, Fun_beta_sor, Bac_beta_sor) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(Group = "non-F1")
      
      nonf1_df %>% dplyr::filter(Sample1 %in% nonf1_hpg_samples, Sample2 %in% nonf1_hpg_samples) %>% dplyr::count()


# nonf1_df <- dplyr::inner_join(fun_nonf1_df, bac_nonf1_df, by = c("Sample1", "Sample2"))
combined_df1 <- dplyr::bind_rows(f1_df, nonf1_df)

# Add metadata and fix Site_pair
combined_df <- combined_df1 %>%
  dplyr::left_join(sample_map, by = c("Sample1" = "SampleID")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Site1 = Site, Clus2_1 = Fun_sor_clus2, Clus10_1 = Fun_sor_clusters) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(sample_map, by = c("Sample2" = "SampleID")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Site2 = Site, Clus2_2 = Fun_sor_clus2, Clus10_2 = Fun_sor_clusters) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Site1_chr = as.character(Site1),
    Site2_chr = as.character(Site2),
    Site_pair = dplyr::case_when(
      Site1_chr == Site2_chr ~ Site1_chr,
      TRUE ~ "Between-site"
    ),
    Site_pair = factor(Site_pair, levels = c("Between-site", sort(unique(Site1_chr))))
  )
```

## Source or sink (F1 - fungal only)

n/a

## fungal cluster dissimilarity as predictor of bacterial dissimilarity

“When two fungal clusters are different (e.g., F1–F2 vs F1–F7), do their bacterial dissimilarities also differ?”

```{r}
# Model: Does fungal dissimilarity predict bacterial dissimilarity?
lm1 <- lm(Bac_beta_sor ~ Fun_beta_sor, data = combined_df)
summary(lm1)
  # Fun_beta_sor has a positive, highly significant coefficient
  # This confirms: fungal dissimilarity predicts bacterial dissimilarity

# Model: Does the relationship differ by fungal group (F1 vs non-F1)?
lm2 <- lm(Bac_beta_sor ~ Fun_beta_sor * Group, data = combined_df)
summary(lm2)
# Interaction term is very significant
# The slope between Bac and Fun βsor is different in F1 vs non-F1
# non-F1 has a stronger slope between fungal and bacterial β-diversity (+0.407 + 0.313 = ~0.72
# F1 has a much weaker slope (+0.407)
# → non-F1 fungal turnover strongly predicts bacterial turnover
# → In F1, this relationship is much weaker — possibly because fungal turnover is minimal



# Model: Add Site effect (control for space)
lm3 <- lm(Bac_beta_sor ~ Fun_beta_sor * Group + Site_pair, data = combined_df)
summary(lm3)
  # Fun_beta_sor and Group still matter even after controlling for site
  # Site explains a huge amount of variation (R² jumps to 0.44), but fungal structure is still predictive of bacterial structure
  # Fun_beta_sor, Group, and Fun_beta_sor:Group are still highly significant
  # The interaction (+0.456) shows the same story: non-F1 coupling is stronger

# Bacterial β-diversity is significantly predicted by fungal β-diversity.
# This relationship is stronger and more consistent in non-F1 fungal communities, while F1 shows weaker, less predictive turnover.

# Bacterial community turnover is significantly and consistently predicted by fungal dissimilarity, with the strength of this relationship varying by fungal subassemblage. Specifically, fungal–bacterial coupling is stronger in non-F1 clusters, while F1 shows high fungal richness but minimal turnover and weak predictive power for bacterial β-diversity — even after accounting for site-level effects

```

We’ve just shown:

Fungal β<sub>sor</sub> predicts bacterial β<sub>sor</sub> (weakly in F1, strongly in non-F1)

But if F1 is compositionally homogeneous (as we know it is) and species-rich, then:

Its β<sub>sor</sub> is low

But we don’t yet know: Is that due to low turnover (β<sub>sim</sub>) or high nestedness (β<sub>sne</sub>)?

And more importantly:

Does fungal turnover (β<sub>sim</sub>) drive bacterial dissimilarity — more than nestedness does?

Better question to test: Is fungal turnover (β<sub>sim</sub>) more predictive of bacterial β-diversity than fungal nestedness (β<sub>sne</sub>)?

```{r load-beta, include=FALSE,eval=TRUE}

# Bac β_sne

  dplyr::rename(Sample1 = SampleID) %>%

  dplyr::rename(Sample2 = SampleID) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample1, Sample2, Bac_beta_sne)

# Join all Bac components to fungal df
df_beta1 <- df_beta_fun %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(bac_sor_df, by = c("Sample1", "Sample2")) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(bac_sim_df, by = c("Sample1", "Sample2")) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(bac_sne_df, by = c("Sample1", "Sample2"))

# Add fungal cluster pair & site pair info
df_beta <- df_beta1 %>%
  dplyr::left_join(sd %>% dplyr::select(SampleID, Clus10 = Fun_sor_clusters, Site), by = c("Sample1" = "SampleID")) %>%

  dplyr::rename(Clus10_2 = Clus10, Site2 = Site) %>%

    Fungal_cluster_pair = ifelse(Clus10_1 == Clus10_2, as.character(Clus10_1),
                                 paste(pmin(as.character(Clus10_1), as.character(Clus10_2)),
                                       pmax(as.character(Clus10_1), as.character(Clus10_2)), sep = "_")),
    Site_pair = ifelse(Site1 == Site2, as.character(Site1),
                       paste(pmin(as.character(Site1), as.character(Site2)),
                             pmax(as.character(Site1), as.character(Site2)), sep = "_"))
  )
```

## Regression using residuals

If fungal cluster identity explains bacterial dissimilarity even after accounting for pool similarity, it strongly supports the idea that fungal communities locally structure bacterial assembly beyond what's available regionally. - By controlling for both the regional bacterial pool (site-level shared species) and fungal dissimilarity (i.e., how different the fungal communities are) — and test whether fungal subassemblage identity still explains bacterial dissimilarity.

```         
- Do fungal subassemblage assignments explain bacterial β-diversity above and beyond what’s expected from fungal compositional distance and shared regional pool?\
```

\

Modeling bacterial dissimilarity as a function of: Fun_beta_sim (fungal turnover) Pool_dist (bacterial regional pool difference between sites)\
\

bacterial turnover \~ fungal + regional pool + cluster identity:

```{r}
lm_base <- lm(Bac_beta_sim ~ Fun_beta_sim + Bac_pool_sim + Fungal_cluster_pair, data = df_beta_wpool)
summary(lm_base)
```

\
isolate the residuals and test the contribution of fungal subassemblages after controlling for pool + turnover:

```{r}
lm_resid_base <- lm(Bac_beta_sim ~ Fun_beta_sim + Bac_pool_sim, 
                    data = df_beta_wpool)

df_resid <- df_beta_wpool %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Fun_beta_sim) & !is.na(Bac_pool_sim)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Bac_beta_sim_resid = resid(lm_resid_base))

lm_test <- lm(Bac_beta_sim_resid ~ Fungal_cluster_pair, data = df_resid)
summary(lm_test)
```

-   We modeled bacterial turnover (β<sub>sim</sub>) residuals, controlling for: 1) fungal turnover (β<sub>sim</sub>) and 2) regional bacterial species pool similarity, then we tested whether fungal cluster pair identity (i.e. transitions between fungal community states) still explains residual variation in bacterial turnover.

-   We calculated R² = 13.2% of the residual variation is still explained by fungal cluster pairing (p \< 2e-16, highly significant overall). We also found many specific cluster pair coefficients are strongly negative and highly significant.

-   Discussion points: These coefficients are the expected change in bacterial turnover (after controlling for fungal β<sub>sim</sub> and regional pool similarity) for each fungal subassemblages pair, compared to the reference level (the intercept), i.e., they quantify the additional, identity-specific effect of transitioning between fungal subassemblages.

Fungal cluster identity still predicts bacterial turnover, even when: - Fungal compositional turnover is already accounted for - Regional species pool differences are already accounted for

This implies that: Not all fungal turnover is equivalent in its effects on bacterial structure

What fungal state the bacterial community in (e.g., F1 vs F3 vs F7) matters beyond how different the fungal communities are compositionally

There's something about the identity of the fungal clusters/emergent properties of their constituent communities — beyond just their dissimilarity — that influences how bacteria assemble.\
\

Now comparing those results those when controlling for fungal total dissimilarity ( as opposed to turnover) and bacterial regional pool total dissimilarity:

```{r}
lm_resid_base2 <- lm(Bac_beta_sim ~ Fun_beta_sor + Bac_pool_sor, 
                    data = df_beta_wpool)

df_resid2 <- df_beta_wpool %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Fun_beta_sim) & !is.na(Bac_pool_sim)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Bac_beta_sim_resid = resid(lm_resid_base2))

lm_test2 <- lm(Bac_beta_sim_resid ~ Fungal_cluster_pair, data = df_resid2)
summary(lm_test2)
```

Total fungal dissimilarity is slightly more influential over bacterial turnover than fungal turnover. Still, not all fungal compositional dissimilarity is equal. The identity of the fungal community state (i.e., subassemblage membership) has predictive power over bacterial turnover beyond what is explained by simple differences in fungal composition or site-level species availability. Said differently: Transitions between specific fungal states leave distinct bacterial signatures, even if the fungal communities are equally dissimilar in total composition or shared taxa. Example: F1_F2 vs F1_F5 Both may have similar β<sub>sor</sub>, but the transition F1 → F2 has a much stronger effect on bacterial turnover than F1 → F5. But this might be where we are seeing a host effect - F2 is only SCSC and F5 has SCSC, BOER, and BOGR.

What about bacterial total dissimilarity?

After controlling for: - Fungal compositional dissimilarity (β<sub>sor</sub>) - Regional bacterial species pool similarity (pool β<sub>sor</sub>) - Plant host identity (Grass_pair)

We modeled the residual bacterial dissimilarity (β<sub>sor</sub>) and asked:

Does fungal subassemblage identity (cluster pairing) still explain variation? - A: yes! 23.1%!\

Emergent properties of fungal subassemblages reveal how fungal communities serve as the architects of bacterial community structure, even after controlling for fungal compositional dissimilarity, the regional species of bacteria, and the plant host identity.

This means: - The identity of the fungal community state, not just its composition or distance, matters for bacterial assembly - Some transitions between fungal clusters lead to consistently greater bacterial restructuring, others to less - This is not explained by host plant or species pool availability

What remains is fungal subassemblage-specific filtering of bacterial turnover

This is our BFI angle... a cross-site, compositional and identity-level signal in bacterial community outcomes. What do we mean by an "identity-level signal"? In this context, we’re distinguishing between:

1.  Compositional dissimilarity (β<sub>sor</sub>) How different are two fungal communities based on species presence/absence?

This tells us how much communities differ, but not who they are.

2.  Subassemblage identity (e.g., F1, F2, F3...) What discrete community state (cluster) is a sample in?

This is a qualitative label that groups communities with similar structure and presumed function or assembly history.

-\> Does the identity of the fungal cluster pair (e.g., F1 vs F3) explain bacterial turnover after controlling for how different those communities are compositionally?

And the answer is yes — substantially so. This is not just a beta-diversity correlation. This is a much stronger ecological statement:

🔹 Two fungal sample pairs with the same β<sub>sor</sub> can have: Very different fungal cluster pairings (e.g., F1 vs F2 vs F3 vs F7)

Very different impacts on bacterial turnover

→ That means the community state itself matters, not just the dissimilarity.

Why fungal identity might matter beyond composition: 1. Functional differences among clusters F1 and F3 may have distinct dominant guilds (e.g., symbionts, decomposers, pathogens)

→ Even if two clusters are equally dissimilar, transitions involving functionally distinct states will have different effects on bacteria.

2.  Differences in ecological assembly rules One cluster might be dispersal-limited, another environmentally filtered

Or one is a stable attractor state, the other a transient stage

These properties can influence how predictable and structured the associated bacterial community is.

3.  Fungal clusters as habitat templates Fungal communities aren’t just biomass — they structure the rhizosphere

They influence carbon flow, exudates, hyphal networks, redox microenvironments

Different fungal states = different bacterial niches, even if compositionally similar

**Implications**: Bacterial community assembly is sensitive to the identity of the fungal biotic environment, not just to compositional gradients or environmental/host context.

This supports the idea that fungal clusters act as filtering regimes — discrete, recognizable, and functionally important community states that structure bacterial turnover.

This identity-level structuring effect is: - Cross-site - Host-independent (controlled for Grass) - Not a compositional artifact (controlled for β<sub>sor</sub>) - Not a biogeographic artifact (controlled for species pool)\
\

What about F1?

-   F1 is:
    -   Widespread

    -   Species-rich

    -   Compositionally homogeneous
-   Despite compositional turnover (β\<sub\>sim\</sub\> ≈ 0.68), it doesn’t drive bacterial turnover as strongly as many other clusters
-   Thoughts:
    -   F1 may be compositionally rich but functionally narrow. The taxa turning over within F1 may be doing the same thing ecologically
        -   → → Bacterial niches remain stable
    -   F1 may lack “driver” fungi - F1 might lack taxa that have strong co-occurrence patterns or ecosystem roles (e.g., ECM, pathogens, strong root-associates)
    -   F1 may dominate in environments that constrain bacterial assembly. Bacterial turnover may be saturated by abiotic structure where F1 dominates
        -   → Less room for fungal variation to matter
    -   F1 may act as a core biome. A stable fungal state with high internal redundancy, widespread across gradients
        -   → Doesn’t *initiate* bacterial change, but might maintain bacterial stability

# Distance–Decay Plots

Pairwise spatial vs ecological distance Regression (linear or exponential decay or loess)

### Spatial distance matrices and decay modeling

#### Methods

To assess **isolation by distance**, we constructed a geographic distance matrix (`GeoDist`) representing the pairwise Euclidean distances (in kilometers) between all sample locations, derived from sample coordinates.

We evaluated spatial structure in ecological dissimilarity by modeling pairwise community dissimilarity (e.g., Bray–Curtis) as a function of geographic distance. This framework quantifies spatial dependence in compositional variation, consistent with expectations under dispersal limitation or spatially structured environmental filtering.

To characterize the form of spatial decay, we fit multiple models, including linear regression, log-linear regression (exponential decay), and non-parametric LOESS smoothing. Model performance was compared visually, and significance of spatial structure was assessed using Mantel tests, which evaluate global correlation between distance matrices [@borcard2018numerical].

Because geographic distance is often correlated with other spatially structured variables (e.g., climate, edaphic gradients, host identity), we first tested the spatial structure of each explanatory distance matrix by modeling it as a function of geographic distance. Where spatial autocorrelation was present, we applied spatial detrending: the explanatory distance matrix was regressed against geographic distance, and the residuals were retained. These spatially detrended explanatory matrices represent the variation independent of spatial position, following recommended procedures for controlling spatial structure in distance-based modeling [@borcard2018numerical].

These detrended explanatory matrices (e.g., climatic dissimilarity, environmental gradients, trait distances) were then used in place of geographic distance to model ecological dissimilarity. This allowed us to test whether non-spatial drivers explain variation in community structure after accounting for the spatial component.

#### Results: Spatial dependence and explanatory dissimilarity

Pairwise ecological dissimilarity increased with geographic distance, consistent with **spatially structured variation** in community composition.\
Mantel tests confirmed significant associations between ecological and geographic distances across all groups (*r* = [...], *p* = [...]), indicating spatial autocorrelation in community dissimilarity.

Decay model fits revealed [linear / exponential / non-linear] patterns depending on group, with [group A] showing [steeper / flatter] decay relative to [group B]. The fitted LOESS models suggested [continuous / threshold-like / saturating] decay in ecological dissimilarity with spatial separation.

Several **explanatory dissimilarity matrices** (e.g., [climate, environment, trait]) also exhibited significant spatial structure when modeled as a function of geographic distance, indicating that spatial position may confound their ecological effects.

To account for this, each explanatory distance matrix was **spatially detrended** using regression against geographic distance, and the residuals were retained. These residualized matrices represent **non-spatial components** of the explanatory variables [@borcard2018numerical].

When these detrended matrices were used to model ecological dissimilarity, we observed [stronger / weaker / similar] patterns relative to models using raw explanatory distances. This suggests that [spatial autocorrelation / non-spatial environmental gradients] explain a substantial portion of the observed ecological variation.

```{r fig-distance-decay-advanced, fig.width=12, fig.height=10, eval=FALSE}
# Create pairwise dataframe from two dist objects
pairwise_decay_df <- function(comm_dist, sd_df, lat_col = "Latitude", lon_col = "Longitude") {
  sample_ids <- rownames(as.matrix(comm_dist))

  # Subset metadata using rownames
  meta <- sd_df[rownames(sd_df) %in% sample_ids, ]
  meta <- meta[match(sample_ids, rownames(meta)), ]

  if (!all(rownames(meta) == sample_ids)) {
    stop("Sample names in metadata (rownames) do not match those in distance matrix.")
  }

  # Get coordinates
  coords <- meta %>%
    select(all_of(c(lon_col, lat_col))) %>%
    as.matrix()
  rownames(coords) <- rownames(meta)

  # Geographic distances
  geo_mat <- geosphere::distm(coords) / 1000  # km
  rownames(geo_mat) <- colnames(geo_mat) <- rownames(meta)

  # Community distance matrix
  comm_mat <- as.matrix(comm_dist)

  # Lower triangle only
  idx <- which(lower.tri(comm_mat), arr.ind = TRUE)

  tibble(
    Sample1 = rownames(comm_mat)[idx[, 1]],
    Sample2 = rownames(comm_mat)[idx[, 2]],
    GeoDist = geo_mat[idx],
    CommDist = comm_mat[idx]
  )
}

# Decay data for all groups
# All samples

# F1 only

# non-F1 only

# Fit + plot decay models
fit_decay_plot <- function(df, group_label, mantel_stat, mantel_p) {
  df <- df %>% drop_na()

  lm_fit <- lm(CommDist ~ GeoDist, data = df)
  log_fit <- lm(log(CommDist + 1e-6) ~ GeoDist, data = df)
  loess_fit <- loess(CommDist ~ GeoDist, data = df, span = 0.75)

  preds <- tibble(GeoDist = seq(min(df$GeoDist), max(df$GeoDist), length.out = 300)) %>%
    mutate(
      Linear = predict(lm_fit, newdata = .),
      Exponential = exp(predict(log_fit, newdata = .)),
      LOESS = predict(loess_fit, newdata = .)
    ) %>%
    pivot_longer(-GeoDist, names_to = "Model", values_to = "Prediction")

  ggplot(df, aes(x = GeoDist, y = CommDist)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.25) +
    geom_line(data = preds, aes(x = GeoDist, y = Prediction, color = Model), linewidth = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Linear" = "blue", "Exponential" = "red", "LOESS" = "black")) +
    labs(
      title = glue("Distance–Decay: {group_label}"),
      subtitle = glue("Mantel r = {round(mantel_stat, 2)}, p = {mantel_p}"),
      x = "Geographic Distance (km)",
      y = "Community Dissimilarity"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
}
```

```{r ignore, include=FALSE,eval=FALSE}
# Convert group to numeric (for correlogram)
```
